item.title: No problem with power rings.
item.content:encoded:
The effect this thing may have in batteries is sure to be amusing. And power draining. I'd like to know what it does on human subjects though… localized entropic decay for lulzombification? Massive ATP dephosphorylation? Re-purposing nerves as cables in order to channel bioelectricity while every cell in your body cannibalizes itself to provide power? Rapid nuclear decay of carbon-based molecules because why the hell not? It doesn't sound all that gruesome. We have seen worst, anyways.

Also, yeah, it looks like is reminiscent of a Green Lantern/Indigo tribe ring, so what? It's practically unusable for anything more drastic than changing your T-shirt's color (rather neat but certainly pointless) and shows incredible potential while almost stating outright it is just not practical. Melting down nuclear reactors in order to bring a person back to life, a D-class no less…

Although I agree that the expungements feel awkward, upvoting because fuzzy feelings and the chance to use this as a way to directly tap into kinetic (I assume) energy from the environment around it. The global warming issue may no longer be an issue with an intelligent usage of this one.

PD: Also, I am picturing a lab coat-wearing wizard raising their ring to the skies and basically causing a storm to reanimate their dead puppy. Call me ridiculous.

I know nothing about anything related to the Green Lantern, so my view of this is objective, and the thing that grabbed me about this article was that it's more science-based than most of the other reality-changing SCP's in that it preserves the conservation of energy law (or whatever it's called) - all actions require some form of energy, and this obeys that law, instead of just breaking the laws of science like so many other things on this site (not that that's a point against said other things). Actually, it kind of reminds me of how magic works in the Inheritance or Young Wizards' series.
Upvoted!
One thing, though: Shouldn't this be classified as "Safe", not "Euclid"? It only activates when a person wears it - lock it in a box and you don't have to worry about it, right?

item.content:encoded: The idea I had when I re-wrote this SCP was that it chemically alters the subject at the molecular level, which would require a massive amount of energy for anything beyond the simplest of tasks. That's why the previous owner of it got himself killed - he was attempting what seemed to him to be a simple thing like "turning lead into gold", not realizing that the energy required to do so would kill him. Similarly, bringing a dead corpse back to life would require re-writing millions of dead cells into a living state, which causes whatever unspeakably redacted event that it did.
